Ireland has issued high temperature warnings. Globally, June 2025 was the second-hottest June on record (16.54°C), behind June 2024 (16.66°C). ECMWF expert Tim Stockdale warns the 2025 El Niño may break records for strength.

Here's what to know about the Legionnaires' disease outbreak on the Upper East Side

clusters.state_of_play: The former Pfizer HQ at 235 E. 42nd St., a 37-story tower undergoing office-to-apartment conversion into over 1,600 units, was found at risk of collapse after structural columns buckled and floors sagged beneath a 10-story horizontal expansion of the building. This triggered evacuation of the building and 148 guests at the neighboring Hampton Inn Grand Central, along with traffic restrictions and closures affecting a busy Midtown stretch near Grand Central for over a day. FDNY drone images confirm the interior damage. The tower has since been stabilized enough for repairs and some residents have been allowed to return. Developer Nathan Berman (MetroLoft) has publicly downplayed the incident, calling it a freak accident limited to a 20-by-20-foot localized section. City records show safety complaints about the building dating to spring 2025, including complaints about falling debris, many of which were dismissed by emergency teams that responded to them. The incident has raised broader questions about NYC's office-to-apartment conversion trend.

items.title: The Superest of all Super El Niños! This year's climate event is on track to break RECORDS for its strength, expert warns

ledger.what_new: ECMWF expert Tim Stockdale warns 2025 El Niño on track to break records for strength.
ledger.unique: Named expert Tim Stockdale (ECMWF) with on-record warning about record El Niño strength.

clusters.state_of_play: Western Europe recorded its hottest June ever, with temperatures 3.06°C (or ~5.5°C by another Copernicus metric) above average, driven by carbon pollution and an exceptionally strong 'Super El Niño'. The UK is in its third heatwave of the year, with UK A&E attendances hitting a record 81,264 in June and school absences in England reaching nearly 20% during the heatwave — June 26 was the highest daily absence rate of the 2025/26 academic year. Wildfires are ravaging France and Spain; a French nuclear reactor has shut down due to extreme heat. Barcelona recorded its highest temperature in 112 years, with some Spanish stations hitting 44°C. Estimates suggest the continent-wide death toll from June's heatwave could exceed 20,000, with ~5,000 excess deaths in Germany alone and thousands more in France, Spain and Belgium. Ireland has issued high temperature warnings. Globally, June 2025 was the second-hottest June on record (16.54°C), behind June 2024 (16.66°C). ECMWF expert Tim Stockdale warns the 2025 El Niño may break records for strength.

clusters.title: What a welcome to NYC: Hampton Inn guests scramble as neighboring tower goes wobbly

items.title: What a welcome to NYC: Hampton Inn guests scramble as neighboring tower goes wobbly

ledger.what_new: Hampton Inn Grand Central evacuated 148 guests due to neighboring tower structural emergency.
ledger.unique: On-the-ground scene: Brazilian World Cup visitors among those evacuated.

clusters.state_of_play: The former Pfizer HQ at 235 E. 42nd St., a 37-story tower undergoing office-to-apartment conversion into over 1,600 units, was found at risk of collapse after structural columns buckled and floors sagged beneath a 10-story horizontal expansion of the building. This triggered evacuation of the building and 148 guests at the neighboring Hampton Inn Grand Central, along with traffic restrictions and closures affecting a busy Midtown stretch near Grand Central for over a day. FDNY drone images confirm the interior damage. The tower has since been stabilized enough for repairs and some residents have been allowed to return. Developer Nathan Berman (MetroLoft) has publicly downplayed the incident, calling it a freak accident limited to a 20-by-20-foot localized section. City records show safety complaints about the building dating to spring 2025, including complaints about falling debris, many of which were dismissed by emergency teams that responded to them. The incident has raised broader questions about NYC's office-to-apartment conversion trend.
